about: Owner-declared entries of the v7 deploy gates (gate_policy.py --declared), read by both v7 policies: policy_v7_rt_mcp.json (POST /resolve, POST /traverse, GET /traverse/capabilities) and policy_v7_rtp_mcp.json (the same routes and POST /pattern). v7 (the owner, 2026-10-18) is v6 with exactly the approved changes: P-edge-0004's pattern text service-side by design (mcp.by_design_checks under pattern.lowercase), the host's /pattern finalisation reserve in budget_respected's arguments (reserve_ms), and absence_scope / strands read via MCP, where the service states them per database (their v6 marks gone; P-scope-0004 / -0006 run on MCP again, so REL-subset-0002 / -0003 are required on mcp as well). The scenarios the rt gate selects are byte-identical to v6's (and v5's) with their warm repeats. What the MCP surface cannot show is classed in the manifest itself, as in v6 (gate_policy derives the exclusions). Declared here, as in v6: one relation the MCP arm can never evaluate because the service refuses one side by design (REL-subset-0007); it lies outside the rt gate's selection, so only the rtp policy reads it. declared_v6_rt.json stays v6's.

relations_excluded.reason: service-side by design (round 2, the owner's decision 4 of 2026-10-16): its side b, P-modes-0004, sends max_contexts 10,001, which the service refuses at submit by the by-design table's case pattern.max_contexts_above_10000 (pattern_out_of_bounds on caps.max_contexts; the host clamps the value to 10,000 and answers, the service never lowers it), so P-modes-0002's partial list can never be held within P-modes-0004's on the MCP arm (the v5 baseline: inconclusive, http 200 / 400). P-modes-0004's own MCP execution stays required as the named by-design case, and the relation stays required on direct-local, where both sides answer.
